info.title: motionEye
info.description:
The HTTP API of motionEye, the one its own web UI uses.

## Signing in

There are two users: the admin, who can change everything, and the normal (surveillance) user, who can watch and download.

Sign in with `POST /login/` and send back the `user` cookie it sets, as the web UI does. Sessions end when motionEye restarts. Requests without one are refused with `403` and `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.

## Conventions

Paths end with a slash. Changes are `POST`, with a JSON body. Many operations answer `200` with an `error` field when they fail, rather than with an error status. Live video comes from motion's own streaming port, not from this API.

servers.description: This motionEye server, including any base path it is served under.

200.description: The user of the session.
Signed in; the `user` cookie set by this response carries the session.

force_password_change.description: True while the admin still has no password; the web UI then asks for one.

429.description: Too many failed sign-ins from this address; wait for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

post.description: Starts a session for the web UI or for a script that keeps cookies. Sessions are kept in memory, so they end when motionEye restarts. Repeated failures from one address are slowed down.

remember.description: Whether the cookie outlasts the browser. False gives a cookie the browser drops when it closes; the session ends on the server at the same time either way.

200.description: The session has ended and its cookie is cleared.
The cameras, each with its settings.

get.description:
Lists the cameras with their settings, as `/config/{camera_id}/get/` returns them. The normal user is not shown admin-only cameras, nor secrets such as passwords.

With `proto`, it instead lists the cameras that can be added from a source, which only the admin may do.

Open to both users.

parameters.description: Discover cameras instead: `v4l2` for local devices, `netcam` for a network camera, `motioneye` for the cameras of another motionEye server, `mjpeg` for a simple MJPEG camera.

parameters.name: scheme
parameters.description: With `proto=netcam`: `http`, `https`, `mjpeg` or `rtsp`.

parameters.description: With `proto` `netcam`, `mjpeg` or `motioneye`: the host.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: With `proto` `netcam`, `mjpeg` or `motioneye`: the path of the URL.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: With `proto` `netcam` or `mjpeg`: the camera login.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: With `proto` `netcam` or `mjpeg`: the camera login.

parameters.name: remote_secret
parameters.description: With `proto=motioneye`: the other motionEye's client secret, from its General Settings. Without it, that server answers that authentication failed.

parameters.name: remote_verify
parameters.description: With `proto=motioneye`: whether to check the other motionEye's certificate.

200.description: The general settings.
Saved; the response has no body.

post.description:
Send the whole object that `/config/main/get/` returns, changed where needed; leave a password empty to keep it. Changing a password ends that user's sessions.

**Requires the admin.**

200.description: The new camera's settings, or an `error`, such as for a remote camera id that isn't a number.

post.description:
Takes one of the cameras found by `/config/list/?proto=…`.

**Requires the admin.**

proto.description: A local video device, a Raspberry Pi camera, a network camera that motion reads, an MJPEG camera shown as it is, or a camera of another motionEye.

path.description: `v4l2`: the device, such as `/dev/video0`. `mmal`: the camera name. Otherwise the path of the URL.

port.description: May be empty, for the default port of the scheme.

username.description: `netcam`: may be empty, for a camera without a login.

camera_index.description: `netcam`: `udp` to read RTSP over UDP rather than TCP.

keep_alive.description: `netcam`: keep the connection open between frames.

remote_camera_id.description: `motioneye`: the camera id on the other motionEye.

remote_secret.description: `motioneye`: the other motionEye's client secret, from its General Settings. Without it, that server refuses the camera.

remote_verify.description: `motioneye`: whether to check the other motionEye's certificate.

200.description: A compressed archive of the configuration files.
Done, or `ok` is false when the archive could not be read.

post.description:
The restored configuration takes effect at once. Where motionEye may reboot the system (its `enable_reboot` option), it reboots instead, and `reboot` is true.

**Requires the admin.**

Changes where the camera itself is read from, not an upload service. For a network camera this sets its URL and login and restarts motion; for an MJPEG camera, its URL; for a camera of another motionEye, its address, client secret and certificate check.

**Requires the admin.**

get.summary: Make a timelapse movie from a group of pictures

200.description: The progress or the key of the movie, or, with `key`, the movie.

key.description: Download the finished movie with it.

progress.description: From 0 to 1 while the movie is being made. -1 once it has stopped: ready when `key` comes with it, failed when it does not.

404.description: No such camera, or no finished movie has this key; make it again.

get.description:
Start it with `interval` and `framerate`, then poll with `check=true` while `progress` is between 0 and 1. At `-1` it has stopped: with a `key`, download the movie with it; without one, making it failed, or the group has no pictures.

Open to both users.

post.summary: Run an action on a camera

200.description: A built-in action answers once it is done, with `error` saying why when it failed. A custom action answers as soon as its command has started, with an empty body; the command's exit status is only logged.

400.description: The camera has no such action, or doesn't save snapshots.

post.description:
Built-in actions:

- `snapshot`: save a picture now. Refused when the camera doesn't save snapshots.
- `eventstart` and `eventend`: start or end a motion event as if motion had been detected.
- `detectionpause` and `detectionstart`: pause or resume motion detection, as the camera's detection button does, for example to disarm and arm an alarm. It changes the running motion and isn't saved: a working schedule takes over again at its next change, and motion's own settings at its next restart.

Any other name runs the camera's custom action script of that name, if it has one, such as `lock`, `unlock`, `light_on`, `alarm_on`, `up` or `preset1`.

Open to both users. The normal user cannot act on admin-only cameras.

parameters.description: The camera id, as listed by `/config/list/`.

admin_password.description: Present, as an empty string, only while the user has no password; left out once it has one. When saving, send a new password, or leave it out or empty to keep the current one.

normal_password.description: Present, as an empty string, only while the user has no password; left out once it has one. When saving, send a new password, or leave it out or empty to keep the current one.

CameraConfig.description: A camera's settings, as the web UI shows them. There are many; the most used are listed here.

proto.description: `v4l2`, `mmal` or `netcam` for a camera motion runs, `motioneye` for one on another motionEye server, `mjpeg` for a simple MJPEG camera.
